rationale: THE RECEIVER WAVE'S FOUR WALKER GAPS, PINNED AS ROWS — the shapes the closure-verifiable residual names (validation/m14/verification/CPP-RECEIVER-TYPING.md §3e, and the 7,913-row named residual the ledger carries as 'second receiver wave (closure-verifiable coverage gap) · 7,913 · ~1.1 %'). WHAT THIS FIXTURE CAN SEE AND WHAT IT CANNOT: the receiver-typing emission has TWO arms. (a) The INDEX arm (BB_CPP_INDEX_CONSUME=1, requires a COMPLETE project index) resolves a receiver from its WRITTEN declaration type — constructor temp, `new`, typed local — and the fixture suite runs WITHOUT the flag, so the suite pins the ROWS (a fix that emitted or suppressed a row would break this file) while the OWNER metadata is pinned by the dedicated red-capable control script/m14/cpp-receiver-wave-verify.ts (complete index over this very fixture; asserts each arm covers exactly its own shapes, the kill-switches are clean, the negative carries no owner, and no arm moves a row). (b) The INDEX-FREE arm (default-ON, kill-switch BB_CPP_LOCAL_RECEIVER=0) anchors a bare call in a member body / `this->m()` against the file's own published members — and TWO shapes here, the OUT-OF-LINE MEMBER BODY (line 18) and the LAMBDA-IN-A-MEMBER-BODY (line 19), are bare calls inside a member body whose class is declared in this file, so the DEFAULT run gives them metadata.owner. This fixture does not pin that metadata (it runs default and asserts no owner state) — cpp/local-implicit-owner does; the index-free arm is merely WHY a reader must not expect 'no owner with the flag off' to hold on lines 18–19 any more. THE SHAPES, one per line of the ruling: a typed local declared where the analyzer's per-function written-type table does not reach it, and a member body whose class scope is not on the scope stack. The measurement that named the gaps says the RANGE-FOR declarator and the MULTI-DECLARATOR'S SECOND NAME are the two the table misses — both were fixed, and in 2026-11 the range-for fix was found to have been silently undone by the KAD2 sameTsNode change (the branch excluded the two fields that actually carry the type and the name); script/m14/cpp-receiver-wave-verify.ts measured 5 of 6 and the branch was corrected, so the control is 6/6 again. THE MULTI-DECLARATOR'S TWO ROWS ARE THE POINT OF THE SHAPE: `Widget a, b;` is ONE declaration with TWO declarators, and a table that reads a single declarator per declaration gets `a` and loses `b` — which is why the verifier checks EVERY row on the line and not the first one.

expectSymbols.name: Widget
expectSymbols.note: the class-like type the whole fixture turns on. It is declared in THIS file so the index built over the fixture holds it, and so the receiver evidence has a real owner to name rather than one nothing owns. THE KIND IS `class` AND NOT `struct` because that is the analyzer's DOCUMENTED C/C++ convention (docs/analyzers/cpp.md: 'classes/structs with bodies -> class'), and the lane's own oracle script/m14/cpp-truth.ts follows it: a C++ struct IS a class in the language's own type system, and the fleet has ONE class-like kind. (The C lane publishes `struct` for a C struct - a different language fact and a different lane's convention.)

expectSymbols.name: draw
expectSymbols.note: the member every shape calls. The index's inheritance-closed member view declares it, which is the condition the receiver-typing emission requires before it will name an owner. The kind is `method` because it is a class member, not a free function.

expectSymbols.name: ok
expectSymbols.note: the second member, so the for-init shape's condition call has a declared leaf too - the condition of a for-init is a call site like any other.

expectSymbols.name: forRange
expectSymbols.note: the RANGE-FOR shape: the range-for's declarator is not a `declaration` node, and the measurement says the per-function written-type table does not reach it — so this row's receiver has no owner today.

expectSymbols.name: forInit
expectSymbols.note: the FOR-INIT shape: the for-statement's initializer IS a declaration node, and the measurement says the table REACHES it — so this shape is the control that says the fix did not have to touch it.

expectSymbols.name: ifInit
expectSymbols.note: the C++98 IF-INIT shape: the init is an init_declarator under a condition node, and the measurement says the table reaches it in this form.

expectSymbols.name: multiDeclarator
expectSymbols.note: the MULTI-DECLARATOR shape: one declaration, two names, and the second name is the one a single-declarator read loses.

expectSymbols.name: outOfLine
expectSymbols.note: THE OUT-OF-LINE MEMBER BODY: the definition is outside the class body, and the class scope has to come from the qualified name. The measurement says the scope reaches it.

expectSymbols.name: withLambda
expectSymbols.note: THE LAMBDA-CAPTURED CLASS SCOPE: a lambda inside a member body, whose own scope is not the class's. The measurement says the scope reaches it.

expectRelationships.note: the range expression — an ordinary call site, and the row that proves the range-for's BODY is walked at all.
THE RANGE-FOR'S RECEIVER ROW. The row is emitted today; what is missing is the receiver evidence on it, and the row must STAY exactly this row when it arrives.
the for-statement's CONDITION is a call site too, and its receiver is the same typed local.
the body's receiver row for the for-init shape.
the body's receiver row for the if-init shape.
THE FIRST DECLARATOR'S ROW — and it is emitted today.

THE SECOND DECLARATOR'S ROW — also emitted today, and also WITHOUT the receiver evidence, because the table read one declarator per declaration. Two rows with the same target and the same line and different receivers: a verifier that checked only the first row would pass a fix that fixed one name and lost the other, which is precisely the shape this case is about.
the IMPLICIT-THIS row: an unqualified call inside an out-of-line member body, whose owner is the class the qualified name names.
the IMPLICIT-THIS row inside a LAMBDA that sits in a member body — the class scope has to survive the lambda's own scope.
the lambda's own call site, which is NOT a member call: its receiver is a local, and no owner may be invented for it.
the class's membership of the member the receiver evidence names.
the class's membership of the second member.
the class's membership of its OUT-OF-LINE definition — the structural fact the implicit-this case relies on.
the class's membership of its out-of-line definition that holds a lambda.
